description:
## Contract risk

calendars-client uses `Option<&[Id]>` for `destroy` and `ids` arguments
across all methods:

- crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/calendar.rs:22-25, 89-93
- crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/event.rs:23-26, 98-102
- crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/event_notification.rs:15-18, 106-108
- crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/participant_identity.rs:12-15, 72-76
- crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/event_parse.rs:14-17

Canonical mail-client uses owned `Option<Vec<Id>>` for `destroy`:

- crate-jmap-mail-client/src/methods/email.rs:108
- crate-jmap-mail-client/src/methods/mailbox.rs:86
- crate-jmap-mail-client/src/methods/identity.rs:81

(For `ids` in `*_get` methods both crates use `Option<&[Id]>`, so the
divergence is on the `destroy` arg specifically — but the broader idiom
is a calendars-client-wide pattern.)

## Why this matters for a caller

Borrowed-slice destroy forces the caller to keep the source `Vec<Id>`
alive across the await:

```rust
async fn cleanup(sc: &SessionClient, dead_ids: Vec<Id>) -> Result<(), ClientError> {
    sc.calendar_set(None, None, Some(&dead_ids), None).await?;
    //                            ^^^^^^^^^^^ dead_ids must outlive this await
    Ok(())
}
```

The canonical owned `Option<Vec<Id>>` lets the caller hand off ownership:

```rust
async fn cleanup(sc: &SessionClient, dead_ids: Vec<Id>) -> Result<(), ClientError> {
    sc.email_set(None, None, Some(dead_ids), None).await?;
    Ok(())
}
```

For top-level call sites the difference is negligible. For composed async
code (fanout, retry loops, helper layers), ownership is friendlier.

The divergence from canonical is also undocumented anywhere I could find —
there's no PLAN.md or doc comment explaining why calendars-client chose
borrowed slices.

## Opinion label

This is borderline taste — the borrowed-slice form is more flexible at the
call site (works on arrays and slices, not just owned `Vec`). The
canonical owned form is friendlier in composed async code. There is no
correctness or completeness issue, only ergonomics.

Filing at P3 with `opinion` label because the engineering basis (lifetime
ergonomics across awaits) is real but minor, and the canonical-template
propagation rule is the strongest argument — and that's a process concern
more than an engineering one.

## Fix shape

Pick one shape and propagate workspace-wide. Either:

A. Change calendars-client `destroy` args to `Option<Vec<Id>>` to match
   canonical. Easy mechanical change.

B. Change canonical mail-client `destroy` args to `Option<&[Id]>`, then
   sweep all extension-client siblings. More invasive but consistent
   with the borrowed-slice idiom calendars-client already uses for `ids`.

Either way, decide once at the workspace level.
